newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA JAN-JULY 15 FOREIGN INVESTMENT FALLS.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA JAN-JULY 15 FOREIGN INVESTMENT FALLS.

text.p: Foreign investments approved by the Indonesian government fell to $16.2 billion in the year to July 15, compared with $21.5 billion in the same 1996 period, a government official said on Thursday.
"Approved foreign investment from January to July 15 fell to $16.2 billion from $21.5 billion," the official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
He said reasons for the decline were not known yet.
The official said 428 projects were approved, including chemical, pulp and steel industries. He gave no futher details.
Indonesian Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo has predicted foreign investments approved by the government in 1997 would be lower than the $29.9 billion in 1996.
